title: Fall of Singapore
summary: After landing in northern Malaya on 8 December 1941, Japanese 25th Army troops crossed to Singapore's northwest coast on 8 February 1942. On 15 February Lieutenant-General Arthur Percival signed the British surrender at the Ford Motor Factory, Yamashita's headquarters, after Yamashita demanded unconditional terms. The Japanese occupation of the island followed.

uncertainty.note: The campaign in Malaya began on 8 December 1941; the fight for the island ran from the landing on 8 February to the surrender on 15 February 1942. Signing time given as 7.50 pm by both opened sources.

as_recorded.value: 15 February 1942; Percival signed the surrender document at 7.50 pm.
The first Japanese troops landed in Singapore on 8 February 1942 via the northwestern coastline.
Japanese 25th Army troops landed at Kota Bahru on 8 December 1941.

where.modern_name: Former Ford Factory, Bukit Timah, Singapore (surrender site)
where.historical_name: Singapore, British-held island; the Ford Motor Factory at Bukit Timah served as Japanese headquarters

importance.justification: The largest British capitulation of the war, opening the Japanese occupation of Singapore and Malaya.
